title: Customer Assurance Lane and Opt-in Replay Instructions
body:
Purpose
This doc is a customer-facing draft for a two-part communication: (A) a short evening status update to publish to the status page + email subscribers, and (B) an optional post-incident ‘assurance lane’ that lets affected tenants opt into a replay and evidence bundle for verification. The goal is clarity, minimal friction for customers who want automatic remediation, and explicit steps for customers who want evidence for compliance or reconciliation.

TL;DR (for status page)
- What happened: transient multi-region latency for inference requests affecting a subset of tenants between 2026-09-18T18:05 and 2026-09-18T20:42 UTC.
- Impact: higher-than-expected per-request latency (tail p99 increased; some streaming sessions truncated) for ~7% of requests routed through the EU region. No data loss observed.
- Current status: degraded -> mitigated; normal routing restored at 20:42 UTC. We are offering an opt-in replay (assurance lane) for tenants who want verified replays and token-level evidence.

Evening status page text (short)
Redwood Inference: Degraded — Partial latency increase (resolved)
We experienced increased inference latency for a subset of EU-hosted requests between 18:05–20:42 UTC on 2026-09-18. Normal service routing returned at 20:42 UTC. If your application experienced persistent slow responses, we offer a replay and evidence bundle to verify outcomes and re-run requests where appropriate. Next update: post-incident summary with timeline and mitigation plan within 72 hours.

Customer email subject (concise)
Redwood update: Resolved latency event in EU (replay option available)

Customer email body (longer)
Hello —
We wanted to notify you directly about an event that affected a portion of inference traffic routed through our EU region on 2026-09-18. The affected window was 18:05–20:42 UTC. During this time, some requests experienced elevated latency and a small fraction of streaming sessions ended early.
What we know now:
- Scope: ~7% of total requests in the EU region; impacted tenant list attached if you opted into detailed notifications.
- Root cause (summary): a controller-side backpressure cascade caused queueing on a subset of GPU pools when a new traffic pattern exceeded expected prefix cache hit assumptions. This caused continuous-batching delays and evictions in KV caches for affected hosts.
- Customer impact: increased p95/p99 latency and truncated streams for some sessions. No user request data was deleted or modified.
- Actions taken: we applied emergency route redistribution to unaffected clusters, tuned queue window thresholds, and enabled a temporary conservative batching profile which reduced latency while throughput stabilized. Full routing normalcy confirmed at 20:42 UTC.

How we will follow up:
1) A detailed post-incident timeline and remediation plan will be published in 72 hours.
2) For customers who need verification, we are offering an "Assurance Lane" (opt-in replay + evidence bundle). See below for how to opt in.
3) We will provide any required compliance artifacts for customers that request them (signed attestation + request/response checksums).

Assurance Lane (opt-in replay + evidence) — what it is
For customers who want us to re-run affected requests (with the exact prompt, model, and pinned model-version where possible) under nominal conditions and provide a signed evidence package, we will:
- Re-run requests during a controlled window in an offline sandbox (no charge for replay runs).
- Provide per-request hashes, timestamps, and checksumed output artifacts so customers can confirm equality or divergence.
- Provide execution environment metadata (model version, quantization profile, routing decision log, region, and deterministic RNG seed when available) and operator notes describing any differences in routing or model variant used.
- For privacy: replays are performed only on decrypted in-memory data; no new external calls or telemetry will be introduced. Replays are only available for requests originating from tenants that opt in.

How to opt in (two choices)
Option A — Tenant self-serve (recommended for engineering teams):
- Send a POST to our replay API endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/replay-requests with JSON body {"start":"2026-09-18T18:00:00Z","end":"2026-09-18T21:00:00Z","include_streams":true}.
- We will respond with a replay ticket id and an estimated completion ETA.
- Expected ETA: 24–72 hours depending on volume and sandbox capacity.

Option B — Customer Success assisted (recommended for compliance/legal teams):
- Reply to this email or open a support ticket and indicate "Assurance Lane opt-in: INC-1429". Provide contact, scope (tenant IDs or application names), and whether you require signed attestations.
- Assigned CS engineer will confirm scope and expected delivery.

Verification artifacts provided
- Per-request request/response checksums (SHA256)
- Replay stdout/stderr logs (redacted for PII)
- Routing decision log excerpt (which model instance / pool / region served the replay)
- Signed attestation document (upon request) with operator verification steps and timestamps

Common questions (FAQ)
Q: Will replays change my billing?
A: No. Replay runs for this incident are free. If you request additional analysis beyond the standard bundle, there may be consulting charges which we will quote up front.

Q: What if the replay output differs from the original result?
A: We will provide a divergence report highlighting token-level differences and potential causes (model variant changes, non-deterministic ops, or runtime rounding). Where feasible, we will attempt a second deterministic re-run with controlled RNG to assess repeatability.

Q: How long will artifacts be retained?
A: We will retain replay artifacts for 90 days by default. If you need longer retention for compliance, indicate that in your opt-in request and we will accommodate with a retention addendum.

Q: Can I request only metadata (no replay)?
A: Yes. You can request just the routing decision logs and per-request checksums without re-running. Use include_replay=false in the API call.

Operational notes for CS / SRE (internal)
- Priority handling: assign a replay ticket label severity=customer-assurance and SLA = 72h for paid customers with enterprise entitlements.
- Sandbox limits: default parallelism 8 tenants; escalate to infra if > 50 replays queued.
- Evidence packaging: use /ops/tools/replay-packager:v1.3 which attaches signed checksums and operator notes.
- Security: replays use customer-specific ephemeral keys; ensure KMS wrapping is enforced.

Draft timeline for external postmortem (public version)
- 48–72 hours: publish redacted timeline + concrete mitigation steps and follow-up roadmap items.
- 7 days: internal RCA complete and engineering remediation PRs opened.
- 30 days: rollout of permanent batching threshold update and KV cache safeguard deployed to all regions.

Notes / writer’s intent and open questions
- This draft is intentionally customer-friendly; technical deep-dive will be in the postmortem.
- Need confirmation from runtime team on: exact list of affected GPU pool IDs, deterministic replay feasibility for all models, and whether model-variant fallback was used for any tenant.
- Legal: confirm whether signed attestation language requires specific phrasing for EU customers.

Next steps for this doc
- Internal review with runtime and legal by 2026-09-20.
- Finalize the short statuspage snippet and queue the email send for 2026-09-18 21:15 UTC.

Contact
If you have questions about the assurance lane or need help opting in, contact your Customer Success lead or reply to this email thread. For operational queries about replay timing, ping @SRE-runbooks.

— Maya (Customer Success)

Draft change log (for internal tracking)
- 2026-09-18: created initial communication draft (Maya).
- 2026-09-19: added API example and evidence list (Aaron).
- 2026-11-21: updated retention policy and added ETA ranges (Sofia).
